condition: firm left sublingual mass over 3 weeks with mealtime enlargement and sharp pain in an adult
level_rationale: A 3-week history of a firm lump under the tongue on the left side that swells up with sharp pain during meals in a 38-year-old adult indicates obstructive submandibular duct sialolithiasis warranting dentist or oral-surgical evaluation for occlusal imaging and stone extraction, whereas that sublingual swelling ballooning rock hard and pushing the tongue upward represents acute floor-of-mouth elevation with impending upper airway obstruction requiring immediate emergency department airway management.

The lump swells up with sharp pain at meals

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg, Ramazani 2022) + 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + unsourced toothache causal belief clause (-att) + single-fact sublingual tongue-elevation airway escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age 38, 3-week firm lump under the tongue on the left side, and mealtime swelling with sharp pain) without naming sialolithiasis or Ludwig angina, with an exact 25-vs-25 word span swap, orthogonal 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing, zero stated negatives, and identical digit multisets across all 8 variants. Under reviewer_notes Rules A and D, SPEC.md section 5.5, and Trend 2, escalating only f3 at the same sublingual site in a separate finite clause to rock-hard swelling pushing the tongue upward shifts care cleanly from dentist management (level 3) to emergency airway care (level 4) without adding unstated body sites, fever bundling, or bleeding.
